methodology.gold_standard_rule: Only HUMAN_REVIEWED primary-source cases may be labelled HISTORICAL_GOLD. Public catalogue or edition metadata are REFERENCE_GOLD and test retrieval/classification, not final historical truth.

cases.source_note: LoC catalogue/edition record identifies Morgan and the sack/burning of Panama; benchmark tier does not claim original-page inspection.
Catalogue description identifies a 20 May 1695 witness statement concerning capture of a ship by Turkish pirates; original archival deposition not inspected by this benchmark.

cases.text_fixture: A corsair vessel was reported offshore, but the record describes no attack, capture, pillage, boarding, ransom, or violence.
A place with a similar spelling is mentioned in a merchant itinerary; no evidence establishes identity with the requested island and no hostile event is described.
piratc raicl capturc 167l appears as corrupted OCR without an identifiable source passage or stable place match.
Three later books repeat the same earlier narrative. They are not three independent source chains.

BnF authority record dates the naval victory of Jean Bart off Texel to 29 June 1694. Catalogue/authority evidence only; original underlying sources not inspected by benchmark.

cases.source_title: Plan de la Ville de Tripoli en Barbarie attaquée par l'Armée navale du Roy
cases.source_note: BnF catalogue record identifies the French naval attack on Tripoli and notes 22 June 1685. Reference metadata only.

cases.source_title: Redención que se ha hecho en la ciudad de Argel este año de 1682
cases.source_note: BNE authority/catalogue data identifies an original manuscript redemption book for captives in Algiers in 1682. Benchmark does not claim folio inspection.

cases.source_title: Papeles sobre Marruecos y plazas de África
cases.source_note: BNE catalogue description includes a 1638 letter about galleys of Algiers and Tunis operating along the coasts of Spain. Presence/operation reference, not proof of a specific attack. This case is retained as a deep-metadata diagnostic because the relevant 1638 galley note is indexed by BNE but not exposed in the current SRU fields returned to the pipeline.

cases.source_title: Relacion verdadera de la presa que las galeras de Venecia han alcançado de las de Tunez y Argel à 13 de Iulio año 1638
cases.source_note: BNE catalogue/digital record explicitly identifies the capture of galleys of Tunis and Algiers by Venetian galleys in 1638. Reference metadata only; original item not yet human-inspected.

cases.source_title: The Buccaneers of America — Letter from the Spanish General / Maracaibo sequence
cases.source_note: Library of Congress exhibition reproduces Exquemelin's Maracaibo narrative and the Spanish general's letter dated 24 April 1669. REFERENCE_GOLD only.

cases.source_title: Panama Canal in Picture and Prose / Exquemelin-derived account
cases.source_note: Library of Congress digitized volume states Morgan's first attack on Porto Bello occurred in 1668. REFERENCE_GOLD only.

TNA education source presents a September 1630 merchant letter; contextual note identifies payment for captains as ransom for captives taken by Barbary corsairs. REFERENCE_GOLD, not original-inspected by this benchmark.
TNA research article states Jan Janszoon relocated to Rabat, became a corsair captain/admiral and was granted the governorship of Rabat-Salé in 1624. REFERENCE_GOLD only.

cases.text_fixture: In 1683 Duquesne led a French naval attack against Algiers in response to corsair incursions. The attacking force is a state navy, so this must not be classified as a pirate attack by the French actor.
cases.source_note: Adversarial classification control: presence of corsair context must not turn a French state bombardment into PIRATE_ATTACK.
